name: Helenium

project_scope.note: The two accepted Helenium amarum varieties are taught inside the species-level learner and are not duplicate species pages. H. quadridentatum remains a provisional installed learner with its range HOLD preserved.

priority: disc-lobe color for H. amarum variety-level training
study_strategy.warning: Start with the stem and leaf architecture before the yellow flower head. H. amarum is unwinged; H. elegans, H. autumnale, and H. quadridentatum are winged.
study_strategy.look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: follow a leaf base down the stem. Is the stem smooth/ridged or does leaf tissue run down it as a distinct wing? Next compare annual versus perennial crown, leaf width/teeth, and the flower head in SIDE view; use a hand lens for disc-floret lobes.
field_sequence: 1. Stem/leaf junction: leaf base decurrent as a wing, or stem merely ridged?
2. Plant base: single-season taproot or surviving perennial crown?
3. Mature leaf: approximate width, edge teeth, and how far the blade runs down the stem.
4. Side view of mature capitulum: disk shape, head profile, ray count and posture.
5. Hand lens: individual disc-floret corolla lobes; compare varieties only with properly documented specimens.

recognition.where_to_look_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: follow a leaf base down the stem. Is the stem smooth/ridged or does leaf tissue run down it as a distinct wing? Next compare annual versus perennial crown, leaf width/teeth, and the flower head in SIDE view; use a hand lens for disc-floret lobes.
shared_morphology: Composite heads (capitula) with marginal ray florets and a raised central disk of numerous tubular disc florets; inspect florets individually rather than treating the head as one flower.
Alternate stem leaves, with species-dependent decurrent bases forming wings along the stem.
Yellow-rayed heads are common but ray color is not a reliable species separator; examine the involucre and mature disk profile.
ordered_field_check: 1. Stem/leaf junction: leaf base decurrent as a wing, or stem merely ridged?
2. Plant base: single-season taproot or surviving perennial crown?
3. Mature leaf: approximate width, edge teeth, and how far the blade runs down the stem.
4. Side view of mature capitulum: disk shape, head profile, ray count and posture.
5. Hand lens: individual disc-floret corolla lobes; compare varieties only with properly documented specimens.
overlap_cautions: H. elegans and H. quadridentatum are both winged annuals; do not separate them using stem wings alone.
H. autumnale and annual winged taxa overlap in yellow rays and winged stems; verify perennial crown and broader toothed leaves.
Disk color varies with flower age and light; do not assign H. amarum varieties from a dark-looking whole-head photograph.
A dried or mowed perennial may appear annual; when basal organs are not visible, leave life-history character unscored.

comparison_matrix.note: Comparisons are structural field cues, not new quantitative measurements. Count ranges and disc-lobe traits require inspected mature material; variation and hybrids/aberrant individuals warrant expert review.

anatomy_lessons.title: 1 · Stem wing versus ridge
anatomy_lessons.plain: A leaf base may continue down the stem as a thin leafy strip; a ridge alone is not a wing.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Photograph the node and 3–5 cm of stem immediately below it, side-lit and with a scale.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: First split H. amarum (unwinged) from the three winged species.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired H. amarum / H. elegans stem-node macros

anatomy_lessons.title: 2 · Annual root versus perennial crown
anatomy_lessons.plain: A perennial regrows from a persistent base, while annuals finish their life cycle in one season.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Show entire basal stem with crown and root attachment; do not infer from plant height.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Helps separate H. autumnale from winged annuals.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired H. autumnale crown and H. elegans annual base

anatomy_lessons.title: 3 · Turn the head sideways
anatomy_lessons.plain: One apparent daisy is a head of tiny florets; the central disk and outer green bracts have diagnostic shapes.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Photograph mature heads in profile at matching magnification with rays and green involucre visible.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Distinguishes globose-profile H. elegans from more elongated-disk H. quadridentatum.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: same-scale H. elegans / H. quadridentatum side-head macros

anatomy_lessons.title: 4 · Count lobes on one tiny central flower
anatomy_lessons.plain: Each tiny tubular flower in the central disk has its own corolla tip; its lobes are not the big outer yellow rays.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Dissect and photograph one mature disc floret with a millimeter scale and clearly resolved lobe tips.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Tests the four-lobed disc-floret character recorded for H. quadridentatum and supports cautious H. amarum variety training.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: H. quadridentatum disc-floret dissection; paired H. amarum variety lobe macros

comparison_cards.title: Bitterweed versus winged sneezeweeds
comparison_cards.separator: H. amarum has ridged but unwinged stems; H. elegans has genuine leafy wings. Check the same node height in both.

comparison_cards.title: Pretty sneezeweed versus longdisk sneezeweed
comparison_cards.separator: Both can be winged annuals. Compare globose versus elongated ovoid/obconic mature heads; inspect disc florets and count rays on actual specimen.

comparison_cards.title: Autumn sneezeweed versus winged annuals
comparison_cards.look_here_first: basal crown and mature leaf margins
comparison_cards.separator: Perennial crown and broader often toothed leaves support H. autumnale; yellow rays and wings alone are shared.
